judgements.greek_church_link: Carried at Widely Accepted. The Apostoliki Diakonia is the Church of Greece's own publishing body, and the page is its published account of its own history. It states both acts that the note uses. The 2018 date is flagged, and nothing after 2010 enters the note. Frazee and Leustean (repo-cited) stay as the named consensus. This is the fix R1-1 preferred. The note's three facts are each on the page. The dropped '35 dioceses' was rightly removed, since the page does not give it.
judgements.american_orthodoxy_links: Plekon is a peer-reviewed article read at the passage. For Russian church to American Orthodoxy, it states the 1970 grant by the Russian Church to the former Metropolia, which is the act and the descent the link claims. With the Tomos and the OCA page it carries Widely Accepted. For Paris to American Orthodoxy ('influenced'), Plekon shows St Sergius-trained Schmemann and Meyendorff going to America and to St Vladimir's, and working there for an American church. It also calls Schmemann a principal architect of the 1970 status. That covers the handoff that Arjakovsky could not, so Widely Accepted holds. Erickson is correctly left as title-only, with no weight on it.
judgements.R1-11_fixed_differently: Agreed. In context, 'Spartas, however, insisted that he wanted to be Orthodox when he welcomed the Ugandan Anglicans' answers Meletios's advice to wait for an Orthodox-Anglican reunion. It does not say Anglicans followed Spartas. The round 1 fix text would have gone past the source. The note now states only what the page shows (raised Anglican; Mukono and Budo; turned to the African Orthodox Church; trustee in 1946). The reason is in a flag.
